name: Nancy Mace
role: U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 1st district (Republican, since 2021); lost the 2026 Republican primary for governor
summary: Nancy Mace is a South Carolina Republican who has moved from a self-described new-voice, bipartisan style (cannabis descheduling, marriage-equality votes, conservative climate caucus) toward a Trump-aligned platform emphasising immigration restriction, sex-based policy on transgender issues, the death penalty, voter ID and tax cuts. She says she is pro-life with exceptions for rape, incest and the mother's life. Her 2026 governor bid, which ended in a fifth-place primary finish, centred on eliminating the state income tax, school choice and enforcing immigration law.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Called for full repeal of Obamacare (2013-2020 statements); no later statement found, and her recent bills reserve federal health benefits for citizens rather than expanding coverage. Said Americans should not forgo care because of cost, so the position is against a state guarantee but not hostile to coverage.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Her 2026 governor campaign centres on eliminating the state income tax with a spending cap, and she backed the 2025 tax-cut law as 'lower taxes'. Neither speaks to the wealthy specifically, but both point against raising their taxes.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted against the 2024 FISA 702 reauthorization because a warrant requirement for searches of Americans' communications failed: 'We cannot, in good conscience, support the government spying on Americans.' She opposes warrantless surveillance, not all surveillance.

limit-guns.rationale: After voting against the 2022 assault weapons ban: 'It's clear gun control and gun bans don't work'; she describes using the banned firearms for hunting and self-defense. Also voted against the 2021 expansion of background checks on private transfers.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2022 voted twice for the Respect for Marriage Act and called marriage 'a basic civil right for any two people'; in April 2025 she repeated 'I voted for gay marriage twice.' In October 2025 she posted 'Adam and Eve, not Adam and Steve', and she has turned against other LGBTQ policies. She has not called for repeal, so this is a mixed record, answered low.

abortion-legal.rationale: Stated at an April 2026 debate: 'I am pro-life with exceptions for rape and incest and life of the mother', which she says matches Trump. She has also backed gestational limits in the 15-20 week range, and her record has varied over time (rape/incest exceptions pushed in 2019). The most recent position is used.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Her bills define protected facilities by 'biological' sex and she introduced the Restoring Biological Truth in Government Act (title only); framing treats sex as fixed. No statement addressing the 'social construct' claim itself.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Her 2026 bills justify entry limits and assimilation screening by harm to American culture and cohesion ('If you import the third world, you will become the third world').

reduce-immigration.rationale: Authored the Third World Immigration Moratorium Act (entry ban on nationals of 39 countries), the Expedited Removal Expansion Act and the 2026 amendment on birthright citizenship: 'entry into the United States is a privilege, not a right.'

nation-first.rationale: On Ukraine aid (Feb 2024) said the administration 'is putting the borders of other nations first rather than our own' and wanted border security addressed first.

open-borders.rationale: Her 2026 entry moratorium and assimilation screening bills, and her statement 'the free ride is over', directly oppose open borders; also supports a border wall.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Her office states 'Israel has a God-given right to exist, to defend itself, and to thrive' and that she voted to send aid to Israel.

school-vouchers.rationale: Supports universal school choice (2026 governor campaign); voucher design is not spelled out in the sources, so medium.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Opposed the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan (2021) and voted against the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act, and warned in 2013 of a 'day of reckoning' over spending. A 2020 survey recorded her as favoring COVID relief spending, so the evidence is not uniform.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Introduced the Preserving Social Security and Medicare for Citizens Act of 2026 and the American Citizenship Healthcare Integrity Act of 2025 (bill titles and sponsorship; texts not read).

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Authored the No Immigration Without Assimilation Act (2026), requiring DHS 'assimilation likelihood' screenings and making unlikelihood to assimilate grounds for denial and deportation: 'We are not a dumping ground for the third world.'

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said in 2013 that 'I don't trust this government; it overreached its boundaries', and in 2025 on congressional stock trading: 'Washington is doing what it always does... something doesn't add up.'

death-penalty.rationale: Introduced the Death Penalty for Child Rapists Act (2026) and the Restoring the Death Penalty in DC Act (2026), covering murder, killing officers and terrorism: 'Criminals need to know there are consequences for their actions.'

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Introduced a constitutional amendment (H.J.Res. 190) limiting birthright citizenship to children with at least one parent who is a citizen, national or lawful permanent resident; not a full descent-only rule.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Introduced the Restoring Merit in the Military Service Academies Act, Restoring Merit in the Military Act, No DEI in DC Act, and a resolution banning race-based caucuses in Congress (titles/summaries only).

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Introduced the PAAW Act (bar NIH funding of research causing significant pain to dogs and cats) and Violet's Law, co-led a bill banning mink farming for fur, and backed a ban on gestation crates.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Her bills target painful experiments on dogs and cats, fur farming and gestation crates rather than animal use as such; no statement found rejecting farming or research altogether. Mixed.

native-born-offices.rationale: Introduced H.J.Res. 188 (natural-born citizenship requirement for certain individuals) and H.J.Res. 194 (bar those with foreign citizenship or allegiance from Congress, courts and other federal posts unless they renounce it). Scope of 188 is not clear from the summaries, so low.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Introduced the Protecting Women's Private Spaces Act (barring 'biologically male' people from sex-specific facilities on federal property), the Prison Rape Prevention Act and the Gender Affirming Child Abuse Prevention Act; says it reflects her view of sex-based spaces ('Women fought for these spaces').

islam-incompatible.rationale: In August 2026 posted that 'Islam must be confronted and Islam must be removed from civil society in the US' and that 'Every single Muslim holding public office in America is a trojan horse'; later said she was speaking about elected officials. Her May 2026 bill also targets belief in religious law operating alongside U.S. law.

term-limits.rationale: Signed a term-limit pledge in 2014 (6 years House, 12 Senate) and said in 2013 that term limits are 'the only way to stop the ruling elitists'. No later reversal found.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Her Protecting Women's Private Spaces Act defines eligibility by biological sex as a fixed category, and she introduced the Restoring Biological Truth in Government Act (title only).

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Her 2026 assimilation bill lists refusal to learn English among views that make an immigrant inadmissible or deportable, and her release says people who refuse to learn English should not come.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Recorded in 2021 as supporting right-to-work laws (vote against the PRO Act, as summarized by OnTheIssues).

voter-id.rationale: Voted for the SAVE America Act in February 2026 (proof of citizenship to register, photo ID to vote) and filed an amendment to start voter ID in 2026: 'Voter ID cannot wait until 2027.'

notes: Positions have shifted: on same-sex marriage (voted for the Respect for Marriage Act in 2022, later posted 'Adam and Eve, not Adam and Steve'), transgender policy (from 'strongly support LGBTQ rights' in 2021 to the 2024-25 bills on sex-based facilities and minors' treatment), abortion exceptions, and Trump (critical after Jan 6, later an ally). The most recent clear position is used. Search budget ran out before police, welfare, energy, tariffs and other topics could be checked; those are null, not negative.
